subject: general
question: A shopkeeper marked his goods in at 25% higher price than their cost price. Finally, he sold the goods at 30% discount on the marked price. His profit/loss percentage is:
solution:
**Given:**

MP is 25% higher than CP

Discount = 30%

**Formula used:**

SP = MP × (100 - L%)/100

L% = L × 100/CP

**Calculation:**

Let CP be Rs. 100x

MP = 125x

SP = 125x × (100 - 30)/100 = 125x × 7/10

SP = 87.5x

Loss = 100x - 87.5x = 12.5x

Loss% = 12.5x × 100/100x = 12.5

**Hence, the required loss is 12.5%**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** As MP is 25% above CP 

CP : MP = 100 : 125

CP : MP = 4 : 5 ------- (1)

Also CP : MP = (100 - D%) : (100 - P)

CP : MP = 70 : (100 - P) ------- (2)

⇒ 4 : 5 = 70 : (100 - P) -- From (1) and (2)

⇒ 4(100 - P) = 350

⇒ 4P = - 50

P = - 12.5

Profit is negative because there is a loss of 12.5%

**∴ T**he required loss is 12.5%
